gen-audiowide-gf-martel-sans: Generous curve openings and a high mean line keep every word of the sans body easy to follow. Martel Sans is built for that quiet legibility, while Audiowide holds one unvarying pen pressure in futuristic, tile-like letters.
gen-audiowide-gf-matangi: Audiowide lays its letters out like tiles with wide grout lines and no stroke contrast at all. Matangi brings hefty, rounded lowercase left open, so paragraphs of sans text feel sturdy and contemporary.
gen-audiowide-gf-maven-pro: Futuristic from the first letter, Audiowide sets the tone. Maven Pro's gentle, uniform line and welcoming open c soften all that tech, and that softening is what makes the pair work.
gen-audiowide-gf-michroma: Michroma gives each letter a wide berth on both sides, with tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips. And Audiowide, with no thin strokes to vanish in glare, gives the headline a crisp, futuristic edge.
gen-audiowide-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre draws wire-weight lines and an s with generous openings, its lowercase standing tall as cast iron capitals. But Audiowide is the one for futuristic flair, while Miriam Libre handles the approachable text.
gen-audiowide-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Crisp and oversized: Mochiy Pop One has a very large lowercase eye and a single stroke width, like laser-cut sheet. And Audiowide's tiled, futuristic letters share that single-stroke discipline, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-audiowide-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One leaves a wide stretch of blank space between letters and carries a sizable lowercase with no brush swell. Next to Audiowide's tiles, a full paragraph here reads clean and friendly.
gen-audiowide-gf-montserrat-underline: Audiowide leads with tall lowercase and tiled, futuristic letters. Montserrat Underline supplies breathing counters, uniform round bowls and oversized lowercase, giving the tech-flavored heading a sturdy sans-serif partner.
gen-audiowide-gf-mozilla-headline: Audiowide cuts its glyphs like strips of equal width, giving a futuristic, tiled look. And Mozilla Headline's big-bodied lowercase and splayed c terminal make the approachable counterweight that holds the pair together.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-bassa-: Almendra Display has a pronounced x-height and letters that never pinch shut, ornate and literary. And Noto Sans Bassa Vah, with its dominant midsection and open-jawed c, keeps long paragraphs contemporary and steady.
